body.text: One of the first questions homeowners ask when they consider professional Christmas light installation is simply, what does this cost? It is a fair question, and it deserves a fair answer, which is that it depends. Not in a vague, evasive way, but in the same way a driveway resurfacing or a roof repair depends on the actual dimensions and condition of the property. A quote for Christmas light installation is built from a handful of concrete factors, and once you understand what those factors are, the range of prices you see across Southern Ontario starts to make a lot more sense.
Why there is no single flat price

Search around for Christmas light installation pricing and you will find wildly different numbers, sometimes for houses that look similar from the street. That is because the sticker price on a display has very little to do with the size of the house and almost everything to do with the length of roofline being lit, the number and size of trees and shrubs receiving wraps, the grade of lighting product used, and how difficult the property is to access safely. A bungalow with a short, simple roofline and no trees will always cost less to light than a two-storey home with dormers, multiple gables, three mature trees, and a steep pitch that calls for a boom truck rather than a ladder.

This is why Festive Holiday Lighting, like most reputable installers, quotes every property individually rather than publishing a one-size-fits-all price list. A phone estimate or a written price with no site visit is a guess, and guesses on a job that involves ladders, rooflines and electrical connections are not the kind of guess most homeowners want their contractor making.
The factors that build a quote
Roofline length

This is usually the single biggest driver of price for a classic seasonal display. Commercial-grade LED C9 bulbs run along the eaves and rooflines in continuous strands, and the total linear footage of roofline being lit is the starting point for almost every quote. A modest bungalow eave might run 80 to 120 feet, while a larger two-storey with dormers, a garage return, and a porch roof can easily exceed 200 feet.
Trees, shrubs and garland

Tree wraps are priced by the tree, generally scaled to trunk height and canopy size, since a mature maple takes considerably more product and labour to wrap evenly than a young ornamental tree. Garland along a porch railing, wreaths on doors and windows, and mini lights woven through shrubs are each added as their own line item, which is why two neighbouring homes with the same roofline length can still land on very different totals once one adds four tree wraps and the other adds none.
Product grade

Festive Holiday Lighting installs commercial-grade LED products built for a full Southern Ontario winter, not the residential-grade strands sold at big box stores each fall. Commercial C9 bulbs and fixtures are more durable, more weather-resistant, and more consistent in colour temperature across a whole roofline, and that durability is reflected in the installed price. It is also why a professionally installed display tends to look cleaner and last through freeze-thaw cycles and January windstorms better than a DIY string bought on sale in November.
Height and access

A single-storey home with a straightforward eave is a different job than a steep two-and-a-half storey roofline with dormers, or a commercial building with a flat roof and a high parapet. Festive Holiday Lighting's crews are WSIB-compliant and carry $5 million in liability insurance, and for taller or steeper work the crew brings a boom truck or lift rather than pushing an extension ladder past a safe angle. That equipment, and the trained operators who run it, is part of what keeps the crew and the property safe, and it is factored into quotes for homes where it is needed.
What a seasonal quote actually includes

A common misconception is that the quoted price only covers the day the crew shows up with a ladder. In practice, the classic seasonal package at Festive Holiday Lighting is a full-season service. It includes an initial design conversation about which rooflines, trees and features to light, professional installation with commercial-grade product, a mid-season maintenance visit to replace any bulb that fails or reset anything a windstorm has knocked loose, complete takedown after January 6, and off-season storage of the equipment. Homeowners are not buying lights they then own and have to store in the garage for eleven months; they are buying a managed seasonal service where Festive supplies, installs, maintains, removes and stores everything.

Because the display is Festive's product start to finish, there is nothing for the homeowner to buy, store, untangle or test each fall. The quote covers the entire season, from design through takedown.
A general sense of the range

Without a site visit, no honest number can be more precise than a general range, but it helps to have a sense of scale. Most Southern Ontario homes fall somewhere between several hundred and a couple of thousand dollars for a full season, depending on roofline length, the number of trees and shrubs included, and the complexity of the roof. A smaller bungalow with a straightforward eave and no trees sits toward the lower end of that range. A larger two-storey home with a complex roofline, several mature trees wrapped, garland, wreaths and a mix of features sits toward the upper end. Commercial properties, municipal and BIA installations, and larger tree lighting projects are quoted separately and can vary well beyond a typical residential range, since the scope, height and equipment involved are usually much larger. The only reliable way to know what your property will cost is a free quote at /contact or a call to (289) 426-5764, where the roofline, trees and access are actually assessed before a number is given.
Permanent lighting is a different cost model entirely

It is worth separating seasonal Christmas light installation from Festive's other service line, permanent lighting. Permanent RGBW LED lighting is installed once in a discreet channel along the roofline and stays there year-round, controlled through a phone app with 16 million colour options and rated to handle Southern Ontario's extremes from minus 40 to plus 60 degrees Celsius. Because it is a one-time installation with a lifetime hardware warranty rather than a service repeated every fall, the cost model looks more like a home improvement than a seasonal rental. Typical residential permanent lighting projects run in the range of 2,500 to 8,000 dollars installed, depending on the length of roofline and the complexity of the trim. For homeowners weighing the two options side by side, our comparison guide on /services/permanent-lighting versus classic seasonal lighting walks through the trade-offs in more depth.
Why booking early matters more than negotiating price

One factor that will not change your price but will change your options is timing. Crews, boom trucks and lifts are booked on a first-come basis through the fall, and by late September the earliest and most flexible installation dates are still open. Booking early does not make the job cheaper, but it does mean more choice over when the crew arrives, more time to plan a design that includes everything you want, and a better chance of an installation date well ahead of the first snowfall rather than a rushed slot in mid-December. Our companion guide on /resources covers the booking calendar in more detail, including why late September is the practical cutoff for best availability.
Why DIY often costs more than it appears to save

It is worth addressing the comparison homeowners naturally make: buying strands of lights at a hardware store and hanging them yourself looks cheaper on paper. In practice, the comparison is rarely apples to apples. Residential-grade lights sold seasonally are not built to the same standard as commercial-grade product, and it is common for a portion of a DIY strand to fail partway through a Southern Ontario winter, whether from moisture getting into a connector, a cold snap stressing the wiring, or a string simply not being rated for the temperature swings the season brings. Add in the cost of a ladder, the time spent untangling and testing strands each fall, the risk of working at height without fall protection or WSIB coverage, and the annual trip to store everything in the garage for eleven months, and the true cost of DIY starts to look less like a bargain and more like an ongoing chore with real safety exposure attached.

Professional installation removes all of that. Festive Holiday Lighting's crews carry $5 million in liability insurance and are WSIB-compliant, which protects both the homeowner and the crew if anything goes wrong on a ladder or lift. The equipment used is commercial grade, chosen specifically for durability through freeze-thaw cycles, and the mid-season maintenance visit catches problems before they become a dark section of roofline on Christmas morning. For many homeowners, the value is not just the finished look, it is not having to think about the display again until the mid-season check happens.
How commercial and municipal quotes differ

Everything above focuses on residential pricing, but Festive Holiday Lighting also quotes commercial properties, municipal and BIA programs, and larger tree lighting installations. These jobs are priced on an entirely different scale, since a shopping plaza roofline, a main street's worth of storefronts, or a large municipal tree can involve far more linear footage, taller structures, and more complex access than a typical home. Commercial and municipal clients also often want features residential customers rarely ask for, such as coordinated colour themes across multiple properties, timed lighting ceremonies, or installations that need to be completed around business hours to avoid disrupting customers. If you are a property manager, business owner or municipal contact exploring options, the same free quote process applies, just scaled to the size and complexity of the project.
Getting an accurate number for your property

The only way to move from a general range to a specific number is a proper assessment of your roofline, trees and access. Festive Holiday Lighting offers free quotes across Hamilton, Burlington, Oakville, Mississauga, Brampton, Milton, Ancaster, Grimsby, St. Catharines and Niagara Falls, and a quote comes with no obligation to book. faq.q: Why can't I get a flat price over the phone?
faq.a: Because the cost is built from your specific roofline length, tree and shrub count, product mix and access difficulty, all of which vary house to house. A number given without seeing the property is a guess, so Festive Holiday Lighting quotes every home individually, usually after a quick look at photos or a site visit.

faq.q: What is included in a seasonal Christmas lighting quote?
faq.a: A classic seasonal package typically includes design, professional installation with commercial-grade LED product, a mid-season maintenance visit, takedown after January 6, and off-season storage. The homeowner does not own or store any equipment between seasons.

faq.q: Roughly how much do most homes in Southern Ontario spend per season?
faq.a: Most residential seasonal displays fall somewhere between several hundred and a couple of thousand dollars for the full season, depending on roofline length, tree count and complexity. A free quote at /contact is the only way to get an accurate number for a specific property.

faq.q: Does a taller or steeper roof cost more to light?
faq.a: Yes, often. Homes that require a boom truck or lift for safe access, rather than a standard ladder, typically cost more because of the equipment and trained operators involved. Festive Holiday Lighting's WSIB-compliant crews use the right equipment for the height and pitch of each roof.

faq.q: Is permanent lighting cheaper than seasonal lights over time?
faq.a: Permanent lighting has a higher upfront cost, typically 2,500 to 8,000 dollars installed, but it is a one-time investment with a lifetime hardware warranty rather than a recurring seasonal service. Homeowners planning to display lights for many holidays, or year-round colour for other occasions, often find the long-term math favours permanent lighting. See /services/permanent-lighting for details.

faq.q: Does booking early get me a lower price?
faq.a: Booking early by late September does not lower the price, but it does secure better scheduling flexibility and access to boom trucks and lifts before the fall calendar fills up. It is the difference between choosing your installation date and taking whatever slot remains in December.
